committeeQuestion.question: If several agents respond to the same liquidity signal, what evidence shows their combined behaviour will not create avoidable payment delays or gridlock?
committeeQuestion.why: BIS Project Agenti is testing how different agent objectives and strategies may affect payment timing, liquidity use and shock propagation in a controlled simulator.
committeeQuestion.evidence: A scenario showing the agents’ objectives, payment priorities, liquidity buffers, common signals, queue effects and trigger for human intervention.

committeeQuestions.question: Which critical payment or orchestration service would stop several agents at once, and can the firm restore minimum service if its normal control plane is unavailable?
committeeQuestions.why: Agent interactions can amplify a shared dependency failure. The test should include containment and recovery as well as prevention.
committeeQuestions.evidence: A dependency map, a tested manual or independent fallback, recovery-time evidence and the named decision owner for switching to minimum service.

committeeQuestions.question: What independent evidence supports the provider’s claims about agent performance, limitations and safeguards in the workflow we plan to use?
committeeQuestions.why: This week’s model launches and Anthropic’s METR arrangement show that capability and access to assurance evidence are changing, while provider claims still need attribution and challenge.
committeeQuestions.evidence: An evaluation report with scope, access limits, tested failure modes, publication terms, unresolved findings and the accountable reviewer.

judgement.title: When agents interact, resilience becomes a system test.
judgement.editorialAngle: Test collective behaviour in shared payment and service systems, where individually controlled agents can still create correlated delays and make recovery harder.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 17 asked whether a firm's evidence could reconstruct one agent's unintended action. Edition 18 moves to the system around the agent: how multiple participants may interact through shared payment, liquidity and service dependencies, and whether the firm can contain and recover from their combined effects.
judgement.observation: BIS’s Project Agenti is testing a controlled payment simulator to examine how agents may affect timing, liquidity demand, gridlock and shock propagation. Japan’s finance minister says G7 leaders agreed to AI-risk tabletop exercises; design and dates are unspecified.
judgement.executiveJudgement: Test interaction, not each agent alone. Controls that work in isolation may still produce correlated delays or disruption to shared services when agents respond to the same signal. BIS is exploring this, not reporting a live failure or setting a supervisory requirement. The Bank of England’s September FPC record links frontier-AI incidents with interconnected cyber and operational risks.
judgement.implication: Ask payments and resilience owners to simulate a common liquidity shock alongside loss of a shared service. Measure payment delays, containment and minimum-service recovery.

weeklyReadout.heading: Can we contain and recover from the combined effects of interacting agents?
steps: BIS is testing payment simulations in which agents represent different system participants.
Several individually controlled agents may still react to a shared signal and shift payment timing or liquidity demand together.
Test a common liquidity shock alongside loss of a shared service, then measure containment and minimum-service recovery.
Assign the first missing recovery step to the payments or resilience owner.

topSignals.title: Agent use is expanding from coding into planning and post-release work
topSignals.label: Agent deployment
topSignals.why: OpenAI's account of Amp describes agent use for planning, design and post-release work. This is a provider-published customer story, not independent proof of general performance; assess the access, usage and review boundaries when work extends beyond coding.

topSignals.title: Repeated shocks make resilience a cross-risk scenario
topSignals.label: Financial resilience
topSignals.why: Andrew Bailey's speech frames financial resilience amid repeated shocks. It is context for scenario design, not a new supervisory requirement; test how correlated financial and operational pressures affect service priorities.
topSignals.source: Primary / Bank of England and Prudential Regulation Authority / 2026-10-08

topSignals.title: A critical BeyondTrust flaw requires an estate exposure check
topSignals.label: Critical vulnerability

topSignals.title: Hosted delivery controls need a tested fallback
topSignals.label: Hosted delivery services
topSignals.why: GitHub Status reports a 12 October disruption across Actions, pull requests and issues, separate from the 7 October incidents in Edition 17. Teams relying on hosted delivery controls should know their release fallback.
